subject: Renewal rollforward: token mix review, latency incidents, and term adjustment proposal
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@helixai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@helixai.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Q3 usage/latency review ahead of renewal

Hi Michael,

Hope you’re well. As our annual renewal window approaches (Nov 1), we wanted to surface two things from Q3 usage and ask for a short ops review:

- Token mix shifted: the percentage of long generation calls (>512 tokens) rose from 8% to ~18% in August/September, driving per-token spend higher than forecast.
- A couple of latency spikes impacted our API SLAs last month (see sample incident in the attached latency_incident_log.pdf).

We’re evaluating whether to: (A) increase committed capacity to smooth unit price, (B) shift critical flows to a lower-latency model variant, or (C) extend the current term with a consumption collar. Can you share any internal analysis on cost impact and recommended actions?

Can we schedule 30 minutes next week to review usage and a proposed term amendment that would let us stage an upsell if latency improves? I’ve cc’d Alex who owns infra at Helix.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lopez
Head of ML Ops, Helix AI

Attachments: latency_incident_log.pdf
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@helixai.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Q3 usage/latency review ahead of renewal

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and the incident log. I pulled a short report (attached token_report_Q3.csv) and a quick summary below:

- Net token spend YTD: 2.1B tokens, Q3 accounted for ~560M (26% of YTD).
- Long generation mix increase drove a ~13% uplift in effective $/1000 tokens compared to Q2.
- Two latency spikes on 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-20 correlated with a backend rollout; those were mitigated by automatic fallback to the stable model at our edge.

Preliminary recommendations:
1) Short term: enable model-variant routing for latency-sensitive endpoints (route to the low-latency quantized variant during peak windows). Minimal code change on your side; we can push routing policy from the Console.
2) Medium term: staged capacity commit — a 6-month step-up commit that buys a lower unit price at scale and includes an SLA uplift during the staged period.
3) Contracts: a consumption collar (monthly true-up band) would give Helix flexibility while preserving pricing predictability for both sides.

I can present these options and cost simulations in a 30-min call. Proposed slots: Tue Oct 6 16:00 UTC or Thu Oct 8 15:00 UTC. Which works?

—Michael
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_report_Q3.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 17:41:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Q3 usage/latency review ahead of renewal

Adding a couple of technical notes we should surface on the call:

- Root cause for the Sept spikes: a kernel rollout that increased tail latency for long sequences on one pool. It was rolled back within 3 hours but impacted Helix because of the request distribution at the time.
- Quick mitigations: prefix caching for recurrent prompts would cut token consumption by 7–12% for their workload profile.
- Cost sim: if Helix accepts a 6-month step-up commit of +20% capacity (baseline as Q3 run-rate) we can offer a blended unit price that nets ~9% savings vs current over that period, plus a one-time onboarding credit.

I’ll prepare a slide with the ops playbook and a suggested canary policy for model-variant routing.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@helixai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Q3 usage/latency review ahead of renewal

Thanks — the summary is helpful. We’d like the call on Thu Oct 8 15:00 UTC. Two asks for the agenda:
1) Walk through the cost sim and the blended price for the 6-month step-up commit (Helix procurement will want firm numbers).
2) Ops playbook: how quickly can prefix caching and variant routing be enabled, and what monitoring will you provide to trigger the staged upsell?

Also, can you put the proposed term amendment in a shared doc? We’ll circulate to procurement before the call.

Sara

On a separate note — Alex: can you share any infra-side limitations before the call so Michael/Karthik can tailor the playbook?
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@helixai.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Q3 usage/latency review ahead of renewal

Great — call confirmed Thu Oct 8 15:00 UTC (invitation just sent). Per your asks:

- Cost sim and blended pricing: attached is a one-page summary in proposed_term_amendment_v1.docx; it shows the 6-month step-up (+20%) with blended unit pricing, projected savings, and the onboarding credit.
- Ops playbook: Karthik will present a runbook for prefix caching + variant routing; expected time to value is 48–72 hours after configuration for the low-friction endpoints. We will also provide a per-route latency dashboard and automated alerts (2x baseline SLA breach triggers an immediate model-variant fallback).

Next steps after the call: if Helix wants to proceed we’ll produce an addendum and a short implementation checklist (SOW optional).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
—Michael

Attachments: proposed_term_amendment_v1.docx
